title: Clickable Flowchart Anatomy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Diagrams; Instructional Design
description: Interactive Mermaid flowchart of the MicroSim drafting process in which every node, branch label and arrow is clickable and fills an information panel with its shape, role, Mermaid source line and style class. A Break it toggle removes the quotes from one label and shows Mermaid's real parse error.

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate the four node shapes of a flowchart and the roles of edges, labels and style classes by inspecting a small working diagram.
prerequisites: Flowcharts as steps joined by arrows

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided inspection of a working artifact with a deliberate break
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Click to inspect, compare shapes, break and repair
keyQuestions: Which node shape marks a decision, and why does only that node have labeled arrows?
What does a style class change, and what does it leave alone?
commonMisconceptions: Node shape is decoration rather than a signal of the node's role.
Quotes around labels are optional in every case.
assessmentOpportunities: Choose the correct shape and write the Mermaid line for a new step
Explain why a label containing parentheses fails without quotes
